newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money rises to 25.0/26.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money rises to 25.0/26.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money rose to 25.0/26.0 percent in active early trading on Friday following a sudden shortfall of liquidity in the money market, dealers said.
They said higher weekly tax payments and the weekend factor could have caused the tightening.
One local bank dealer said money operators were caught by surprise as some state banks emerged as borrowers in the market.
"When people saw state banks turning up in the market, the rate began to rise because this usually indicates tight supply," he said.
Dealers said the problem could be temporary because operators could switch to short-term securities (SBPUs) to obtain liquidity from the central bank.
However, the local bank dealer said the short-term market focus would be on Tuesday tax payments.
Overnight swap rates rose to 2.75/2.90 from 1.25/1.75.
Dealers said longer-term swap rates edged up slightly on the back of tight conditions.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 11.29 percent, compared with 11.65 percent on Wednesday.
